newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bond fund inflows up sharply -- survey.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bond fund inflows up sharply -- survey.

text.p: U.S. bond funds showed a sharp rise in cash inflows and equity funds showed a more modest increase for the two-day period ended February 3 compared to the three-day period ended January 30, Mutual Fund Trim Tabs reported Wednesday.
U.S. stock funds took in $1.19 billion in cash for the two-day period, compared to $1.05 billion for the three days ended January 30, according to funds followed by Mutual Funds Trim Tabs.
Bond funds showed inflows of $983 million versus $22 million.
The fund tracker said aggressive growth funds saw a slowdown to inflows, to $273 million from $432 million, while growth funds posted inflows of $351 million, up from $250 million.
Growth and income funds had inflows of $491 million, up from $427 million, while international funds recorded inflows of $164 million, down from $407 million.
Muni funds recorded inflows of $618 million versus $11 million, while government/GNMA funds posted inflows of $65 million versus outflows of $120 million, it said.
Corporate/income/global funds showed inflows of $114 million versus $18 million.
